clue.text: Enlargement of the heart

parts.note: the heart of the word 'the' is its middle letter, and enlarging that letter means spelling its name out in full

explanation.walkthrough: The medical reading is the decoy: 'the heart' is the central letter of the word 'the', and the 'enlargement' is that letter's written-out name.
explanation.definitionFit: The spelt-out name of a letter is a longer form of the single character, hence an enlargement of it.

clue.text: Transatlantic mail goes on one vessel of old Brittany

parts.note: chain mail is armour, spelt the American way across the Atlantic
I is the Roman numeral one
a can is a container or vessel

explanation.surface: Post from America travels on a single ship of ancient Brittany.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'mail' is chain mail, not post; American spelling drops the U.
explanation.definitionFit: Armorica was the Roman name for the region of north-west Gaul that became Brittany.

clue.text: When Alice could never enjoy the White Queen's jam

definitions.text: When Alice could never enjoy the White Queen's jam

parts.words: When Alice could never enjoy the White Queen's jam
parts.note: in Through the Looking-Glass the White Queen offers jam tomorrow and jam yesterday but never on the present day

explanation.walkthrough: Lewis Carroll's White Queen rule: 'jam tomorrow and jam yesterday, but never jam' on the present day.
explanation.definitionFit: The rule names the present day as the one time the jam is never given.

clue.text: Putting something right, of course

parts.note: putting is the golf stroke on the green, and getting the ball right into the cup on a golf course

explanation.walkthrough: 'Putting' looks like setting, but it is the golf stroke; 'course' is a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: Finishing a golf hole means sinking the ball in the cup, typically with a putt.

clue.text: Support clergy going on the stage, perhaps

indicators.note: one piece goes on after the other, so the clergy word follows the support word

parts.note: to back someone is to support them
the cloth is a collective term for the clergy

explanation.surface: Someone urges backing for clergymen who want to act in the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going on' sets clergy after support. 'The stage, perhaps' is meant as a setting or background, which is what a painted cloth at the rear of a theatre gives.
explanation.definitionFit: A painted backcloth hung at the rear of a theatre forms the scenery, the setting in which a play happens.

clue.text: A couple of drinks for the motorist

definitions.meaning: glasses filled to the brim, plural so more than one
the guards on the front and rear of a car

explanation.walkthrough: Bumpers are brimming glasses; the plural is matched by 'a couple of'.
explanation.definitionFit: A brimful glass is a bumper, and cars carry protective bars of the same name.

clue.text: May, fall for a' piece of mischief

parts.note: may and can both express permission
to trip is to stumble and fall

explanation.surface: A girl called May tumbles over in a prank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May' looks like the month or a name, but it is the verb of permission. A cantrip is a Scots word for a spell or trick.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots a cantrip is a witch's spell or a playful trick.

clue.text: Spiteful race found in islet

indicators.note: the race letters are found inside the islet word

parts.note: a cay is a small low island
TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A nasty contest takes place on a small island.
explanation.walkthrough: TT goes into CAY. The TT is a famous motorbike race held on the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiteful, malicious remarks are described as catty.

clue.text: Refractory at best — in love, possibly

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, the letter O

indicators.note: possibly means the letters of the preceding words could be arranged differently

explanation.surface: Someone describes being in love as at best stubborn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'love' is the tennis zero; 'possibly' shuffles 'at best in' to follow it, and the surface's lover is a decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Refractory means stubborn and unmanageable, resisting control.

clue.text: Was informed of talking animals!

indicators.note: talking signals that the word for animals is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a herd is a group of cattle or other animals

explanation.surface: Someone learnt of beasts that can speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'talking' signals a sound-alike of HERD.
explanation.definitionFit: To have been told of something is to have heard of it.

clue.text: A hearty sort of, trader?

parts.note: hearty is read as being at the heart, the centre, so a trader who stands in the centre between two parties

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearty' looks like jovial, but here it means placed at the heart: a dealer who sits between producer and buyer.
explanation.definitionFit: An intermediary dealer buys from producers and sells on, standing between the two parties in a chain of trade.

clue.text: Ship in produce of China for her

indicators.note: the ship abbreviation sits in the middle of the Chinese crop

parts.note: tea is the famous crop grown in China
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: A cargo vessel is loaded among the tea chests for some woman.
explanation.walkthrough: SS goes into TEA. 'her' defines a woman's first name, a convention for names in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a woman's given name, so it can stand for a particular she, a 'her'.

clue.text: Material is light, with no backing

parts.note: a ray is a beam of light

indicators.note: backing means the word no is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fabric is described as weightless and without any lining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' and 'with' are links; 'Material' looks like an adjective but names a fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an artificial silk fibre made from cellulose and woven into cloth.

clue.text: Layer of odds meets another, perhaps — for a lark ?

definitions.text: Layer of odds meets another, perhaps — for a lark ?

parts.words: Layer of odds meets another, perhaps — for a lark ?
parts.note: a lark is a songbird that sings at dawn, and a person up at dawn is named after such birds; bookmakers meeting at first light suggest one such riser

explanation.walkthrough: A 'layer of odds' is a bookmaker; 'for a lark' looks like 'for fun' but a lark is someone who rises at dawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who gets up very early is called a lark, after the bird that sings at dawn.

clue.text: Cases in which the horse is not racing, but backed ?

definitions.text: Cases in which the horse is not racing, but backed ?

parts.words: Cases in which the horse is not racing, but backed ?
parts.note: a working horse is backed into the shafts so the wagon is on it, a picture that splits the box word into wagon plus on plus s

explanation.walkthrough: 'Backed' looks like a racing bet, but a cart-horse is backed into the shafts: the cart's on.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardboard boxes used for packing are cases.

clue.text: Just a method we'd understand immediately:?

parts.note: just means right, as in a fair decision
a way is a method of doing something

explanation.surface: A fair approach is one everyone would grasp at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we'd understand' is a link that also hints the solver should get it at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Straight away, without delay.

clue.text: Conjurer's incomplete request to Swiss scientist

indicators.note: incomplete means the conjurer's opening words lose some letters at their end

parts.note: the conjurer's request in a card trick is 'pick a card'; this word supplies its opening 'pick a'
the request ends on the object asked for, the card

explanation.surface: A magician calls out half a line to a Swiss researcher.
explanation.walkthrough: The conjurer's request is 'pick a card'; 'incomplete' cuts K and A from 'pick a'. Auguste Piccard was a Swiss physicist famous for balloon and bathyscaphe voyages.
explanation.definitionFit: Auguste Piccard was a Swiss physicist and explorer of the stratosphere and the deep sea.

clue.text: Footsore, if led astray in a rural area

parts.note: a corn is a painful hard patch of skin that makes the foot sore

indicators.note: led astray means the letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A walker with aching feet is misled while out in the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'astray' rearranges IF LED into FIELD; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A field of growing grain is a piece of farmland in the countryside.

clue.text: Showed that underworld chief took part

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld
to play is to take part

explanation.surface: It was revealed that a gang boss was involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'underworld chief' suggests a crime boss, but it is Dis, Roman ruler of the dead; 'that' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Exhibited or put on view.

clue.text: Nullifies directions with stage setting

parts.note: N and E are the compass points north and east

indicators.note: setting means the letters of stage are arranged in a new order

explanation.surface: A theatre director's instructions about scenery cancel each other out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stage setting' reads as theatre scenery, but 'setting' is the signal to rearrange 'stage'; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To cancel or annul something is to nullify it.

clue.text: Drink for Swinburne's sister ?

definitions.meaning: to drink is to gulp down
Swinburne's poem Itylus opens '..., my sister, O sister ...', addressing the bird

explanation.walkthrough: Swinburne's poem Itylus addresses the bird as 'my sister'.
explanation.definitionFit: To gulp down liquid, and the bird hailed as sister in Swinburne's poem Itylus.

clue.text: Church workers-sidesmen, perhaps ?

definitions.meaning: officials who look after a church and lead processions
a verge is a side or edge, so people at the verge are, humorously, men at the side

explanation.walkthrough: Sidesmen are real church ushers, so the second reading poses as a near synonym, but it plays on verge meaning an edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Both readings describe people: caretakers of a church, and folk at the edge or margin.

clue.text: He calls for some armour-that's about it

indicators.note: about means the armour word goes around the other piece

parts.note: a visor is the face guard on a helmet, part of a suit of armour

explanation.surface: A man asks for some armour and that is the whole request.
explanation.walkthrough: VISOR goes about IT; 'for' and 'that's' are links. 'calls' means pays a visit.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who calls pays a visit, a guest at the door.

clue.text: Variety of fabrics alarms' tie-makers

indicators.note: makers are those who form something new, so the letters are made into a fresh word

explanation.surface: Cloth manufacturers who produce neckties have a range of cloth that is alarming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makers' rearranges ALARMS and TIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloths and textiles of different kinds are collectively called by this plural.

clue.text: A liquid note ?.

definitions.meaning: a tiny unit of fluid measure, about a drop

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one liquid (flowing) note, but it is two meanings: a fluid measure and a musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: A minim is both a drop-sized apothecary's measure of fluid and a half note in music.

clue.text: Sail, going 'with the navy

definitions.meaning: a small sail set above the topgallant
the British navy is the ... Navy

explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Navy is Britain's navy; a royal is also a high square sail.
explanation.definitionFit: A high square sail on a sailing ship, and the word that pairs with Navy in Britain's fleet name.

clue.text: " The — gift' of beauty (Byron)

parts.note: a line from Byron's Childe Harold about Italy, with one word left out

explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank: Byron's Childe Harold calls Italy's beauty a deadly gift.
explanation.definitionFit: Byron's phrase calls beauty a deadly gift, the word that fits the gap.

clue.text: Drink to. divine, youth leader!

parts.note: DD is Doctor of Divinity, a divine being a clergyman

indicators.note: leader means only the first letter of youth is taken

explanation.surface: A toast is raised to a holy young leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divine' is a noun, a clergyman, abbreviated DD; 'leader' takes Y from 'youth'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot drink of spirits, sugar and water.

clue.text: Down town display of fresh lines.

parts.note: fresh means new
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a set of lines

explanation.surface: A dejected place shows off a newly written poem.
explanation.walkthrough: Down here is County Down in Northern Ireland, which holds this town; 'display of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Newry is a town in County Down, Northern Ireland.

clue.text: Modern if unusual way to treat Lady

indicators.note: an unusual way of arranging means the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A contemporary, if odd, approach to looking after a noblewoman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual way to' rearranges TREAT and LADY; 'if' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Of the present or recent age, as opposed to former times.

clue.text: Blossom not sure to appear?

definitions.meaning: hawthorn bloom, which comes out in late spring
split in two, the words mean might bloom, a flower that is not certain to come

explanation.walkthrough: Split into two words, the answer says it might flower, so is not sure to appear.
explanation.definitionFit: Hawthorn blossom is known by the name of its spring month, and 'may flower' means might bloom.

clue.text: Nymph in some boring poster?

parts.note: something dry is dull and boring
AD is short for advertisement, which a poster is

explanation.surface: A water sprite appears on a dull advertising bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in some' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A wood spirit of Greek myth that lives in trees.
